findings.title: An over-cap plan is run in full with no human choice
quotes: lines, ok = plan(root, slug, gate, add, pick)
findings.fix: in `step`, when `len(names)` is over the cap and `pick` is not given, return plan's `run:` and `choices:` lines plus `next: show the human the choices, then nio jury next ... --pick <lens,lens>`. Write nothing.

sources.situation: more lenses are planned than `jury.max_runs` allows (for example `--add` pushes the plan past the cap). `plan` returns its lines with `ok` True and says "over the cap: the human chooses what runs". `step` only refuses when `ok` is False. It then reads the lens names and `_begin` writes a pack and a `run <lens>:` line for every lens. The orchestrator launches them all in parallel and spends the cost the cap exists to bound. The human's choice is skipped and nothing flags it.

findings.reason: `plan` (jury.py ~311-336) returns ok True when over the cap and only prints the "human chooses" line and choices. `step` (1393-1410) returns early only when `not ok`, and `names` then go straight to `_begin`/`packs`. Nothing in `step` checks the cap or waits for `--pick`.

findings.title: `--add` reason text can invent a lens that gets a pack and a juror line
quotes: names = re.findall(r"([a-z][a-z-]*) \(", next(x for x in lines if x.startswith("lenses: ")))
findings.fix: get the lens names from `plan` directly (return the dict, or a structured line) instead of parsing display text. At the least, check each name against `agents.load(root)`.

sources.situation: `nio jury next ... --add "consistency:D-1 changed (see spec)"` makes the display line `consistency (D-1 changed (see spec))`. The regex also matches `changed` as a lens. `missing` in `plan` was computed from the real lenses, so no card check fails. `_begin` writes `packs/changed.md` and a `run changed: card nio-changed` line for a card that does not exist. The orchestrator either fails or invents a juror, and `collect` is told to expect a lens nobody can answer. The same parse exists in `collect`, but `step` now feeds the result into pack writing.

findings.reason: `step` line 1399 parses the display line `lens (why)` with the regex `([a-z][a-z-]*) \(`. A reason such as "D-1 changed (see spec)" also matches `changed (`. `missing` in `plan` is computed from the real lens dict, so the false name passes the card check and `packs` writes `packs/changed.md` plus a `run changed:` line.

findings.title: A `--run` value is only checked to be a directory
findings.fix: require `re.fullmatch(r"R-[\w-]+", run)` before the `is_dir` check, and raise the same `no run` error otherwise.

sources.situation: `--run ..` or `--run ../../somewhere` passes, because those are existing directories. `packs()` then does `mkdir(parents=True)` and writes `jury/packs/*.md` and `step.json` under that location. `Accepts: --run an existing run folder` is not enforced. A mistyped or model-generated run name can write pack files outside `.nio/runs/R-*`.

findings.title: Run reuse does not check the slug and trusts every `step.json`
findings.fix: add `slug` to `step.json` and compare it. Treat an unreadable `step.json` as no match.

sources.situation: `step.json` is `{"gate", "round", "version", "lenses"}`, with no slug. A run started for another effort at the same gate name, round and version string, with no outputs yet, is returned by `_reusable`. This is plausible at implementation gates such as `implementation-E-1` when two efforts share a commit. Its packs, written for the other slug, are then handed out as this slug's. Separately, `json.loads(p.read_text())["gate"]` on a truncated or old-format `step.json` raises `JSONDecodeError` or `KeyError`. Every later step without `--run` then crashes on that file.

findings.title: A pack that exists is never refreshed, so a stale `nio check` can reach jurors
findings.fix: when `step.json`'s version differs from `version_now`, rewrite the packs and `step.json`. Or refuse with `next: start a new run`.

sources.situation: packs are written, then the artefact is edited, for example a quick fix after the first `step`. The orchestrator calls `step --run <run>` again, and the run still has no `<gate>-*.md` output. `packs()` keeps every old `<lens>.md`, with the old `0 errors` or `N errors` check output, and `step.json` keeps the old version. Jurors judge the new files against a check result for the old text, and nothing says so. The reuse rule compares versions, but this explicit-`--run` path does not.

findings.title: The spec-gate consistency juror is given worker instructions it cannot follow
quotes: - Before editing a file not covered here, run: nio query --path <file>
You may write only your output file, named at the end; you can't run commands.
findings.fix: build the spec-gate memory with the juror instructions (`worker=False` or a juror flag) and add the same "you can't run commands" sentence the implementation-gate pack has, or state that the juror's reply, not the file, carries `memory-used`.

sources.situation: a juror at the spec gate gets the consistency pack built by `_pack_text`. That pack's memory section ends with the worker's `## How to use this` block, which tells it to run `nio query --path <file>`, to write a change request first (`@nio:remember`), and to end its reply with `memory-used:`. Its output rule says to write the whole output to one file and to no other, and the implementation-gate pack says it cannot run commands, but the spec-gate pack says neither. So when the juror finds a spec requirement against an approved record, it is told to write a change request it has no right to write and to run a command it cannot run. The juror check that D-261024-zbne says juror packs carry is never given to it.

findings.reason: `_pack_text` (jury.py 1330) calls `memory.build(root, asked)` with the defaults `worker=True` and `diff=None`. pack.py line 80-81 then appends the WORKER "How to use this" block. The implementation-gate pack in evidence.py 622 has the "you can't run commands" sentence; the spec-gate pack has no such text.

findings.title: The implementation-gate "run only next" case also prints a run line
quotes: only `next: nio jury evidence <slug> E-n --run <run>, then nio jury next <slug> <gate> --run <run>`, no pack written
findings.fix: return only the `next:` line in that case, or amend CT-1 to list the `run:` line.

sources.situation: at an implementation gate whose run has no `results.json`, CT-1 says the step prints only the `next:` line. `_begin` returns a `run: <run>` line first, so the output differs from the contract. The test `test_ac12_step_at_the_implementation_gate` checks only the last line, so nothing catches the extra line. The run ID is already in the `next:` line, so the extra line is not needed.

findings.title: Escalation loop on a grill-deferred or CLI blocker
quotes: for l in dict.fromkeys(s["lens"] for s in f["sources"]):
findings.fix: skip lenses not in `names` (the planned lenses) in the escalation loop, as `changed()` skips `deferred` and `cli`, so the step falls through to `check`.

sources.situation: at the spec gate a Deferred point marked "contradiction" becomes a finding with `validation` "confirmed", `severity` "blocker", `status` "open" and a source whose lens is `deferred`. No juror ever has lens `deferred`, so the `< 3` count is 0 and `step` returns "next: escalate deferred: run 2 more jurors ..." on every call. `check` is never reached, so no outcome is composed and the human is never shown the list. The same happens at an implementation gate for a blocker whose source lens is `cli`.

findings.reason: jury.py 672-677 creates a contradiction Deferred finding as blocker, confirmed and open, with source lens `deferred`. No juror carries that lens, so the escalation loop's `< 3` count in `step` (1432-1438) is 0 and it returns "escalate deferred" on every call, before `check` at 1439. `changed()` already skips `deferred` and `cli` (445), which shows the case is known but not handled in `step`.

findings.title: AC-2's "verdict record written once" is not what the test asserts
quotes: assert verdict_count(root) == before, "rerun records no verdict"
findings.fix: reword AC-2 to say a rerun writes no new record, and assert `verdict_count` equals 1 after the rejected step.

sources.situation: AC-2 says the outcome is "composed and recorded", with a "verdict record written once". `check` records only approved, rejected and human outcomes, so a rerun records nothing. The test pins that, which contradicts the AC's wording. It also does not check the prior `rejected` record is present exactly once. Either the AC text or the test is wrong, and neither says which.

findings.title: AC-2's test asserts the opposite of the AC's "recorded" observable
quotes: verdict record written once; one pack file per lens to re-run
findings.fix: Settle whether `rerun` writes a verdict record. Then change the AC text to say none is written, or change the test to assert exactly one record.

sources.situation: AC-2 says the outcome is "composed and recorded" when it is `rerun`. The test asserts `verdict_count(root) == before, "rerun records no verdict"`. The pack half of the AC is proven. The "record written once" half is not proven, and the test asserts the reverse. In `jury.step`, `check(record=True)` runs before the rerun branch. Whether `check` writes a record for `rerun` is not shown in the pack. The AC and the test cannot both be right.
